title: Pure curve fibres and finiteness of a flat horizontal marking
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $Z\to T$ is flat and finitely presented. Suppose $X_\eta$ and $Z_\eta$ are dense in $X$ and $Z$, respectively [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $X_\eta$ is nonempty and irreducible of Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $Z_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-residue-field], possibly empty. Then $f$ is surjective, every geometric fibre of $f$ is nonempty and pure of dimension one, and $Z\to T$ is finite, flat and finitely presented with every nonempty geometric fibre pure of dimension zero. Pure dimension $d$ means that every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] has Krull dimension $d$; a geometric fibre is a fibre followed by extension of its residue field to an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. If $Z_\eta$ is empty, then $Z$ is empty.

source.place: Tags 0GSJ and 0GSK, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional and remark-flat-equidimensional (second list, with F=O); Tag 02LS, lemma-characterize-finite. Morphisms Tags 02NK and 0397, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d and lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0. Retained parent proof Steps 7--8.

proof.text: Put $g=f\circ i:Z\to T$. A closed immersion is proper, and proper morphisms compose, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c),(a); thus $g$ is proper. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], both $f$ and $g$ are locally of finite type. Flatness of both and finite presentation of $g$ are hypotheses.

Properness makes $f(X)$ closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The nonempty generic fibre gives $\eta\in f(X)$ by the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Since $\overline{\{\eta\}}=T$ by [def-sc-generic-point], $f(X)=T$. For every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] makes $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ surjective. The target has a point, hence this geometric fibre is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01W1, definition-proper; Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective. The closed-image argument is the definition of a generic point.

proof.text: The nonempty irreducible space $X_\eta$ has itself as its unique irreducible component by [def-weil-irreducible-components], so its components all have dimension $1$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] to $f$ with $d=1$: the base $T$ is integral, $f$ is flat and locally of finite type by Step 1, and $X_\eta$ is dense by hypothesis. Every nonempty geometric fibre is pure of dimension $1$. Step 2 gives its nonemptiness.

source.place: Tags 0GSJ and 0GSK, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional and remark-flat-equidimensional, second list with F=O_X; geometric clause from Morphisms Tag 02NK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $Z_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$. The residue field of the unique base point is $\kappa(\eta)$ by [def-weil-residue-field], so its fibre is $Z_\eta$ itself by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Thus $|Z_\eta|$ is discrete. By [def-weil-irreducible-components], an irreducible subset is nonempty; it cannot contain distinct points $a,b$, since its intersections with $\{a\}$ and the complement of $\{a\}$ would be two proper closed subsets covering it. Its maximal irreducible subsets are therefore singletons. In a singleton the only nonempty irreducible closed subset is the whole space, so the chain supremum of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is $0$. If $Z_\eta$ is empty, there are no components and the same universal assertion holds.

source.place: Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field (2), applied over the field kappa(eta). Component dimension is the elementary discrete-space calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] again, now to $g$ with $d=0$. The base is the same integral $T$; $g$ is flat by hypothesis, locally of finite type by Step 1, and its generic fibre is dense by hypothesis. Step 4 supplies the component dimensions. It follows that every nonempty ordinary fibre $Z_t$ and every nonempty geometric fibre of $g$ is pure of dimension $0$.

source.place: Tags 0GSJ and 0GSK, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional and remark-flat-equidimensional, second list with F=O_Z; Morphisms Tag 02NK for geometric fibres.

proof.text: For each $z\in Z$ put $t=g(z)$. The fibre homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] gives a unique point $\widetilde z\in Z_t$ mapping to $z$; in particular $Z_t$ is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], $Z_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is locally of finite type. Step 5 gives dimension $0$ for every component of this fibre. Thus [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], with $Y=O=Z_t$ and $n=0$, gives local topological dimension $0$ at $\widetilde z$. This holds for every $z\in Z$, so the reverse implication of [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] makes $g$ locally quasi-finite. Since $g$ is proper by Step 1, [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes $g$ finite. Its flatness and finite presentation are hypotheses, and Step 5 supplies the geometric-fibre assertion. If $Z$ is empty, the pointwise criterion is vacuous and the same implication still applies.

source.place: Morphisms Tags 01T4 and 0397, lemma-base-change-finite-type and lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0; Varieties Tag 0A21 (5), lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic; More on Morphisms Tag 02LS, lemma-characterize-finite (3) implies (1).

proof.text: Finally, if $Z_\eta=\varnothing$, its image in $Z$ is empty. The assumed density says that the closure of this image is all of $Z$, whereas the closure of the empty subset is empty. Therefore $Z=\varnothing$. This also checks the empty marking case of Steps 4--6: component and pointwise conditions are vacuous.
